events.title: Charlemagne dies at Aachen
events.description: The Frankish king, crowned emperor in 800, died after ruling much of western Europe. His empire was divided among his grandsons within thirty years, but its memory shaped the Holy Roman Empire.
events.html: The Frankish king, crowned emperor in 800, died after ruling much of western Europe. His empire was divided among his grandsons within thirty years, but its memory shaped the Holy Roman Empire.

events.title: Robert de Comines, Earl of Northumbria, is killed at Durham
events.description: Robert de Comines, briefly Earl of Northumbria, was killed in Durham. His violent death was one of the key events that led to the Harrying of the North, William the Conqueror's campaigns of 1069–1070 to subjugate northern England.
events.html: Robert de Comines, briefly Earl of Northumbria, was killed in Durham. His violent death was one of the key events that led to the Harrying of the North, William the Conqueror's campaigns of 1069–1070 to subjugate northern England.

events.title: Henry VIII dies at Whitehall
events.description: Henry VIII died aged 55 after a reign that broke with Rome, dissolved the monasteries and saw six marriages. His nine-year-old son succeeded him as Edward VI.
events.html: Henry VIII died aged 55 after a reign that broke with Rome, dissolved the monasteries and saw six marriages. His nine-year-old son succeeded him as Edward VI.

events.title: Galileo observes Neptune without recognising it
events.description: Galileo's notes record a 'star' near Jupiter that was in fact Neptune, and even note that it seemed to move. The planet was not identified until 1846.
events.html: Galileo's notes record a 'star' near Jupiter that was in fact Neptune, and even note that it seemed to move. The planet was not identified until 1846.

events.title: Gas lamps light Pall Mall in London
events.description: Frederick Albert Winsor's demonstration lit part of Pall Mall with gas lamps, the first public street lighting by gas. Gas lighting spread rapidly through British cities over the next decades.
events.html: Frederick Albert Winsor's demonstration lit part of Pall Mall with gas lamps, the first public street lighting by gas. Gas lighting spread rapidly through British cities over the next decades.

events.title: Paris capitulates and France signs an armistice with Germany
events.description: After a four-month siege, the French government agreed an armistice with the new German Empire. The peace that followed cost France Alsace and much of Lorraine.
events.html: After a four-month siege, the French government agreed an armistice with the new German Empire. The peace that followed cost France Alsace and much of Lorraine.

events.title: Japanese forces attack Shanghai
events.description: Japanese marines clashed with China's 19th Route Army in Shanghai, and Japanese aircraft bombed the Zhabei district. The fighting lasted over a month before a ceasefire was brokered.
events.html: Japanese marines clashed with China's 19th Route Army in Shanghai, and Japanese aircraft bombed the Zhabei district. The fighting lasted over a month before a ceasefire was brokered.

events.title: Space Shuttle Challenger breaks apart after launch
events.description: Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after lift-off, killing its seven crew, including teacher Christa McAuliffe. A faulty seal in a booster rocket was to blame, and shuttle flights stopped for 32 months.
events.html: Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after lift-off, killing its seven crew, including teacher Christa McAuliffe. A faulty seal in a booster rocket was to blame, and shuttle flights stopped for 32 months.
